chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a cup of water was brought to him containing a silver clasp; I saw him removing it with his teeth.

key_terms.ضَبَّةٌ: A clasp or cover, typically on a drinking vessel

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq do with the silver clasp on his water cup?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of the prohibition against consuming food or drink from gold and silver vessels, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence (*fiqh*). By removing the silver clasp (*zipbah*) with his teeth, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrated that the restriction applies to the material of the vessel itself, allowing for the consumption of beverages from mixed-material cups after removing the precious metal component. This incident underscores the distinction between the vessel's material and the act of drinking, reinforcing the etiquette (*adab*) of avoiding extravagance in daily habits.
